tips.title: Seam Line Removal on Fuselage Halves with Tamiya Extra Thin
tips.text: After gluing fuselage halves with Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, clamp them and let cure for 30 minutes. Run a bead of liquid cement along the seam inside the fuselage with a fine brush — the melted plastic slightly squeezes out, creating a weld bead. After 24 hours, sand the seam with 400 grit, then 800 grit sanding sticks. If a visible line remains, apply a thin layer of Vallejo Plastic Putty, let dry, and sand again. Finally, restore any lost surface detail (rivets, panel lines) with an RB Productions scriber.

tips.title: Assembling Multi-Part Gun Barrels with Trumpeter and AFV Club
tips.text: Use Tamiya Plastic Cement for Trumpeter and AFV Club gun barrels. Apply a small dot of cement to the joint, then press parts together. Clamp with a vice grip for 10 minutes. For tight tolerances, use a Tamiya 0.5mm scribing tool to adjust misalignment. For AFV Club parts, use a 0.2mm brass pin to align barrels before gluing. Always dry-fit first to ensure parts fit without force.

tips.title: Wing Alignment Jigs for Arma Hobby and ICM Models
tips.text: Create a wing alignment jig using a Tamiya 0.8mm scribing tool and a block of basswood. Mark wing mounting points on the jig and align each wing section by pressing the Tamiya scribing tool into the basswood. This ensures consistent wing angles and spacing. Use a Tamiya Plastic Cement for bonding, and apply a small bead along the wing root for added strength. For ICM models, use a 0.2mm brass pin to ensure precise pivot points.

tips.title: Installing Photo-Etch Parts with Eduard and Clear Prop Models
tips.text: Use a Tamiya 0.1mm scribing tool to bend Eduard and Clear Prop photo-etch parts. Apply a small dot of Tamiya Plastic Cement to each joint, then press parts into place. For delicate parts, use a Tamiya 0.5mm scribing tool to carefully shape and fit. Always dry-fit before gluing to avoid damaging thin metal. Use a Tamiya 0.2mm pin to hold parts in place during drying.

tips.title: Assembling Tracks with Individual Links vs. Vinyl or Workable Kits
tips.text: For individual link tracks (e.g., Tamiya), use Tamiya Plastic Cement and assemble each link with a 0.2mm pin to maintain alignment. For vinyl tracks, use a Tamiya 0.5mm scribing tool to cut and fit sections. Workable kits (e.g., ICM) require a 0.2mm scribing tool and a Tamiya 0.5mm scribing tool to shape and fit. Always test fit sections before gluing. Use a Tamiya 0.8mm scribing tool for final alignment adjustments.
